newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA HIT BY INJURY CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA HIT BY INJURY CRISIS.

text.p: Australia's tour of Britain and Ireland suffered a double-blow on Friday when two key players -- Jason Little and Michael Brial -- were ruled out for at least three weeks and possibly the rest of the tour.
They were the second and third major injury setbacks for the Wallabies who have already sent home lost test lock Garrick Morgan after he fractured an ankle in the opening tour match in Italy.
Little and Brial were seriously injured in Wednesday's victory over Scotland A prompting Wallaby officials to fly out Owen Finegan and Adam Magro to join the squad as replacements.
Little, with 38 caps at centre, suffered medial ligament damage and would miss the test against Scotland on Saturday week and the Ireland test two weeks later.
"He may be out for up to four weeks, so technically he'll be ready and is hoping to be back for the Welsh test," team doctor John Best told Reuters.

But the extent of the injury make his chances of recovery for the Welsh test on December 1 very remote, leaving him only a shot at Australia's last match a week later against the Barbarians at Twickenham.
Little missed most of Australia's domestic season with a broken collarbone and facial injuries, but was on the verge of regaining his test place with two strong performances in tour matches.
The full extent of Brial's ankle ligament injury will not be known until Wednesday when a decision will be taken whether to send him home.
The 26-year-old backrower, who has 10 test caps, would be out of action for at least three weeks, Best said.

Australia's run of injuries continued at training on Friday when lock David Giffin suffered a hamstring strain, ruling him out of Saturday's fixture against Combined Scottish Districts in Glasgow. Warwick Waugh has been named as his replacement.
Best said Giffen's injury was only minor.
